articles.title: Tech Outages Surge Worldwide Amid AI-Driven Security Shift
articles.summary: A surge in tech outages worldwide is attributed to the increasing influence of artificial intelligence on digital defense and security.
articles.content: Reports are emerging of a surge in tech outages worldwide, sparking concerns about the resilience of modern digital infrastructure. Experts say these incidents have routine explanations, but they also point to a growing trend: AI is increasingly influencing the dynamics of digital defense and security. Researchers attribute this shift to the proliferation of AI-assisted vulnerability discovery, which has unleashed a flood of software bugs that attackers are then exploiting with AI tools at an unprecedented pace. As a result, organizations face intense pressure to rapidly patch their systems, leaving IT teams struggling to keep up with the sheer volume of updates. The rapid pace of technological advancements has created a perfect storm for network failures. Flawed updates in infrastructure can have far-reaching consequences, as seen in Microsoft's recent 365 outage. A combination of factors contributed to this issue, including other network failures that exacerbated the problem. The NSA has also been affected by a similar issue. Its internal communication system went offline due to botched patching following critical PHP updates in October. This highlights the strain on systems caused by the need for rapid updates and patches. The consequences can be severe, disrupting essential services. Internal updates are also causing problems for other major tech companies. Apple has reported snafus related to an internal update, further underscoring the challenges of keeping pace with technological advancements. These issues demonstrate that even well-resourced organizations can struggle with the demands of maintaining secure and up-to-date digital systems. The accumulation of "tech debt, a result of cutting corners on upgrades and maintenance, has become a significant concern for many organizations worldwide. This practice, though often tolerated in the past, now poses a greater risk due to increased external pressures and bugs in patches. The increasing reliance on artificial intelligence (AI) in IT administration has led to a growing trend of accelerated evaluation and preparation for updates, but experts warn that human analysis and planning are still essential components of the process. While AI tools can provide valuable support, they cannot replace the need for human understanding of what went wrong and whether the patch addresses the underlying issue. In fact, many IT administrators are now relying on AI to augment their work, rather than automate it entirely. The use of AI in cybersecurity is becoming more widespread, but its limitations should not be overlooked. As one expert notes, current AI tools are still unable to replicate human analysis and planning, highlighting the need for a combination of both human insight and technological support. Despite these challenges, there is growing optimism that AI acceleration will eventually help defenders get on top of common vulnerabilities and better secure software in general, leading to a decrease in background noise and new security threats. The sheer scale of vulnerabilities being uncovered has reached a staggering milestone this week, with over 100,000 identified in 2026 alone. In comparison, just four years ago in 2022, there were roughly 25,000 recorded vulnerabilities, highlighting the exponential growth in the number of potential security risks. This year's total is even more striking when considered alongside previous years: it has already surpassed the combined totals for both 2024 and 2025, with still over a month to go before the end of the year. The recent disclosures by researchers using AI have shed light on critical vulnerabilities in a range of software systems, including PHP, NGINX, and Java. The recent spate of outages across various industries has highlighted a disturbing trend: the increasing reliance on software systems that are inherently vulnerable to bugs and glitches. Researchers have been warning about these vulnerabilities for some time now, but it seems their warnings are finally being heeded. Meanwhile, in another development, JPMorgan Chase has confirmed that hackers have breached its security systems in a separate incident. The attackers gained access to certain marketing data held by third-party vendors, which may include sensitive customer information such as names and email addresses. While the bank downplayed the severity of the breach, it acknowledged that some company data was stolen. Visa and Mastercard have also been affected by similar attacks against their vendors. It's a worrying trend that highlights the need for better security measures across the financial industry. The fact that these incidents are not linked to the recent outages is cold comfort, as it suggests that there may be more vulnerabilities waiting to be exploited. Police in the Netherlands have recently foiled several attempts at violence directed towards customers of digital bank Revolut. While the motives behind these attacks are unclear, they follow a disturbing trend of physical assaults on wealthy cryptocurrency holders who are forced to hand over money while being held hostage. A court ruling has compelled the UK government to acknowledge that it instructed Apple to bypass its own encryption and access customer iCloud data. This admission follows a long-standing dispute over the extent of government powers in accessing sensitive information. British officials had previously refused to confirm or deny the existence of a technical capability notice" issued under British laws, which are designed to keep such notices confidential. articles.title: Missile Strike Hits Kryvyi Rih, Leaving Two Dead and Scores Injured
articles.summary: A missile strike hit the Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih on Friday night, killing two people and injuring dozens.
articles.content: A devastating missile strike has rocked Kryvyi Rih, the hometown of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, leaving two people dead and scores injured. Local officials reported that a 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman were among those killed in the attack on Friday night. The city's administration head, Oleksandr Vilkul, confirmed the casualties via Telegram, while regional military administration head Oleksandr Hanzha revealed that six children were among the 60 wounded. The strike caused significant damage to infrastructure and property in Kryvyi Rih, with four fires reported and around 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools, an industrial facility, as well as businesses and vehicles affected. Vilkul described the destruction, noting that entire neighborhoods were severely impacted by the attack. The missile assault on Kryvyi Rih aligns with Moscow's pattern of retaliatory measures in response to high-profile Ukrainian attacks, such as this week's strikes on the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Crimea. In southeastern Poland, European troops are participating in a two-week military exercise that started on November 9. The unusual deployment of forces is part of preparations for a potential post-conflict mission in Ukraine aimed at stabilizing the country and rebuilding its military. The joint operation has heightened tensions between Europe and Russia, just as the US attempts to gain momentum in peace talks that it is facilitating to end the war that began with Russia's invasion of Ukraine nearly five years ago. The development has sparked alarm among European countries who are concerned about what they see as Moscow's efforts to destabilize the continent. In a separate development, US President Donald Trump discussed the conflict with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping during a summit in China on Thursday, according to his envoy Steve Witkoff. The conflict between Russia and Ukraine continues to escalate, with devastating consequences for civilians on both sides. A missile attack in Zelenskyy's hometown in central Ukraine has claimed the lives of two people and left scores wounded. The Ukrainian leader himself weighed in on the situation, warning that describing Russian President Vladimir Putin as anything less than an enemy could undermine international pressure on him to end the conflict. In other parts of Ukraine, a Russian drone attack on a five-story apartment building in Kharkiv region injured 11 people, including two children, while another attack on Kyiv's capital left one person wounded. Meanwhile, local officials in Russia reported that Ukrainian drone strikes had wounded three people in the Bryansk and Belgorod border regions. The war between Ukraine and Russia shows no signs of abating, with both sides suffering losses and civilians caught in the crossfire. articles.title: P-8 Poseidon aircraft face challenges in detecting submarines during NATO exercises
articles.summary: The Royal Air Force pilots rely on advanced sensors and sonobuoys to detect submarines, but harsh weather conditions can complicate these missions.
articles.content: A challenging task lies ahead for Royal Air Force pilots when their hours-long mission to hunt a submarine finally comes to an end. The P-8 Poseidon aircraft relies on advanced sensors and sonobuoys to detect submarines lurking beneath the surface of the sea during NATO exercises like Dynamic Merlin, which simulates real-world anti-submarine warfare scenarios. Those who have flown with RAF P-8 crews know that the hunt for a submarine can be an arduous task, requiring multiple flights per week at low altitudes just a few hundred feet above the water's surface. The pressure is on to locate and track the target before it disappears. Rough weather in the Baltic Sea area and northern Scotland, particularly during winter months, can significantly complicate these missions as well as the return journey to RAF Lossiemouth base. Weather conditions in the Baltic Sea area can be particularly challenging for P-8 Poseidon missions, forcing aircraft to navigate through rough seas and strong winds during winter months. The Poseidon's capabilities are impressive, equipped with advanced radar, cameras, electronic support equipment, and acoustic sensors that allow it to track submarines effectively. However, even this robust technology is not immune to the effects of harsh weather. Low-altitude flying is essential for releasing sonobuoys, which rely on being close to the surface to detect noise or emit sound waves that bounce back off targets. The aircraft can carry up to 129 of these devices. Flying at such low altitudes exposes the crew to turbulence and icing conditions, which can significantly impact their comfort and ability to perform tasks during a long mission. The P-8 Poseidon aircraft is designed for sub-hunting missions, but bad weather can make these flights even more challenging. Turbulence, wind, and rough seas can complicate an already demanding task of locating a submarine that's expertly hidden beneath the waves. A recent flight was described as one of the busiest sorties by crew members, with a complex weather forecast involving wind, storms, and high sea states. This required extra planning before takeoff, which added to the mission's complexity. The crew had to depart from Lossiemouth using a shorter runway, limiting their fuel capacity. As a result, they were forced to stop in Sweden for refueling en route to the exercise. P-8 flights are already physically and mentally demanding on crew members due to long hours and intense focus required during the mission. Even landing back at base can be a challenging part of the day for these pilots. The 10-hour flight time was taxing on the crew, adding to their physical and mental exhaustion. The days are indeed long for P-8 pilots, who liken their work to a marathon rather than a sprint. The demands of P-8 Poseidon sub-hunting missions extend far beyond the hours spent searching for a target. The final approach to base can be just as taxing as the initial hunt, requiring pilots to remain focused and alert. According to Group Capt Kevin Latchman, deputy assistant chief of staff in No 11 Group, which oversees RAF global air operations, the last five minutes of the flight can be equally crucial as the search itself. "So they are very challenging missions," he added, highlighting the complexity of these operations. The relentless pace of P-8 Poseidon sub-hunting missions makes them a marathon rather than a sprint, testing the endurance and concentration of pilots to the limit. articles.title: Home Cooking Fires Pose Significant Risk During Thanksgiving
articles.summary: Unattended cooking is the leading cause of home cooking fires and fire fatalities, according to the NFPA.
articles.content: Thanksgiving is just around the corner, and for many of us, it's a time to come together with loved ones and enjoy a delicious holiday meal. However, this festive occasion also poses a significant risk to households across the country. According to Susan McKelvey, communications manager at the NFPA, unattended cooking is the leading cause of home cooking fires and fire fatalities. This stark reality should serve as a timely reminder for all of us preparing our Thanksgiving feasts to remain vigilant in the kitchen. As we go about preparing our holiday meals, it's essential that we keep a close eye on the stove and surrounding areas, especially with multiple guests vying for attention. Having fire safety equipment readily available can make all the difference in preventing and containing a kitchen fire. In addition to a working fire extinguisher, it's crucial to have one or more fire blankets on hand to smother small blazes before they spread. To avoid accidents, maintain a safe distance between cooking equipment and combustible materials. The three-foot rule applies not only to items like potholders and dishtowels but also to kids and pets who should be kept at least three feet away from the range and areas where hot food or drink is being prepared or served. To minimize risks, keep pot and pan handles turned towards the back of the stove. This simple precaution can prevent accidents caused by bumping, catching on clothing, or being pulled down by a curious child or pet. Leaving the house unattended while cooking can be a recipe for disaster, especially during holidays when there are more distractions. If you must step out, it's crucial to take precautions against kitchen fires. Turning off the oven before you leave is a simple yet effective measure that can prevent accidents. In case of an oven fire, keeping the door closed and turning off the heat is essential; this will starve the flames of oxygen and help contain the blaze. If the situation worsens and flames start to escape from the oven chamber, it's time to evacuate immediately and call emergency services for assistance. Asteroid Apophis to Pass Within 19,000 Miles of Earth in April 2029
articles.summary: Astronomers are excited about the close encounter between asteroid Apophis and Earth, which will be visible to the naked eye and provide valuable data on small bodies in our solar system.
articles.content: Asteroid Apophis is expected to make its closest approach to Earth in mid-April 2029, passing within a distance of approximately 19,000 miles. This close encounter will be about 12 times closer than the moon and even more so than many satellites that orbit our planet. The asteroid's proximity to Earth has astronomers excited, as it will also be visible to the naked eye, making for a rare celestial sighting. In recent decades, significant advancements have been made in predicting such asteroid flybys, thanks to space probes providing valuable data on small bodies in our solar system. Astronomers now possess increasingly reliable and detailed information about potentially hazardous asteroids like Apophis, allowing them to better track their movements. However, despite this progress, the ability to respond to an impending threat remains a pressing concern for scientists and policymakers alike. The key challenge lies not in detecting asteroids but in developing effective planetary defense technology that can alter their orbits instead of relying on destructive measures. Astronomers at Kitt Peak Observatory discovered Didymos, an asteroid spanning 780 meters, nearly three decades ago. This celestial body was found to have a smaller companion, Dimorphos, which orbits it approximately every 12 hours. The discovery of the "moonlet" was made by Czech astronomer Petr Pravec a few years after the initial sighting of Didymos. The paired asteroids presented an ideal testing ground for planetary defense systems, requiring deflection techniques to alter their trajectories. This scenario led NASA to identify them as suitable targets for a crucial experiment. The Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission was subsequently launched in late 2021. A year after its launch, the DART probe collided with Dimorphos at a speed of over 13,000 miles per hour. Scientists had anticipated that this impact would reduce the orbital period of the mini-moon by a minute or more, but the actual outcome was significantly different. The collision resulted in a decrease of only 33 minutes in Dimorphos' orbit around Didymos. The observed deviation from their expected trajectory was largely due to the ejection of debris during the impact. This led to a much greater recoil effect than what would have been produced by the impact alone. As a result, not only was Dimorphos affected but also the orbital speed of both asteroids around the sun decreased. The aftermath of the DART mission's collision with Dimorphos has led to a series of unexpected effects on its orbit and that of its parent asteroid Didymos. The debris ejected by the impact has created a long tail behind Dimorphos, effectively transforming it into a comet-like object. However, questions persist regarding the long-term consequences of this event. As scientists continue to analyze the data from the DART mission, they are left wondering about the broader implications for asteroid dynamics and planetary defense strategies. In October 2024, the European Space Agency (ESA) launched the space probe Hera on a mission to study both Dimorphos and Didymos up close. After flying by Mars in November, Hera began its approach phase and took its first image of the asteroids from about 800 miles away. Hera's detailed images of Didymos were released early this month, marking an important milestone for the mission. As it enters the vicinity of the asteroid pair, Hera will conduct a thorough examination of both bodies to shed light on their formation and evolution. Hera's upcoming flyby of the asteroid pair offers scientists an unparalleled opportunity to study crater formation in greater detail. By examining the impact site where NASA tested its planetary defense systems, researchers can gain insights into the complex processes that shape the surface of asteroids. A crucial aspect of this investigation is determining the exact mass of Dimorphos, a key factor in evaluating the effectiveness of the DART mission as a testbed for planetary defense technology. This information will provide valuable context for understanding the dynamics at play during the impact event. The precise mass of Dimorphos will also help scientists better comprehend the asteroid's properties and behavior. The Hera probe is equipped with a range of instruments designed to capture a wealth of data on the asteroids. A lidar instrument will allow researchers to create detailed topographic maps of the surface, while others will investigate the chemical composition of the material. Furthermore, high-resolution images of the asteroids are expected, taken at a resolution of 1 meter per pixel. In addition to its scientific payload, Hera carries two miniature CubeSats, Juventas and Milani, which will be deployed in January 2027. These compact satellites, often used for simple experiments or student projects, will attempt to land on the surface of Dimorphos. The Hera probe is equipped with a gravimeter to measure changes in Dimorphos' gravity due to its parent asteroid Didymos during orbit. Simultaneously, the probe will conduct an in-depth analysis of the surface composition of both asteroids, searching for signs of dust and volatile substances often found within space rocks. articles.title: New Zealand Day Tours Offer Comfortable Transportation Options
articles.summary: A traveler took day tours to explore the South Island's vast landscape without navigating unfamiliar roads.
articles.content: As I arrived in New Zealand after a 17-hour flight from New York City this May, I was eager to make the most of my first visit to the country. My travels took me around the North Island, where I indulged in Auckland's vibrant food scene and stayed at the innovative Hotel Britomart. Visiting Wellington's Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa was also a highlight. However, as I ventured into the South Island, I realized that its points of interest are far more dispersed due to the massive Southern Alps that need to be navigated through. The island's wide-open roads seemed daunting for an American like me who is accustomed to driving on the "wrong side. My solution to exploring the vast and beautiful landscape without worrying about navigating unfamiliar roads was to book a series of day tours with reputable operators. I had tried this approach before, having used it on all six continents during my travels. One such tour that caught my eye was an Arthur's Pass train tour starting in Christchurch, as well as a Walter Peak farm tour in Queenstown. The moment we boarded the Sprinter van for the day trip to Milford Sound, I was struck by the comfort and luxury it offered. Each of the 14 black leather seats came equipped with a gray lambswool blanket, a plush green pillow, and a bottled shot of Manuka ginger Vitamin C boost juice. As someone who's always on the lookout for natural energy boosts while traveling, this amenity caught my eye immediately. I've tried numerous ginger shots around the world, but this one was particularly enticing. Our guide provided context about Milford Sound's history, ecosystems, and Indigenous Māori connections during the five-hour journey each way, making the time pass more quickly. The van was equipped with Starlink Wi-Fi, allowing passengers to stay entertained on their screens while we traveled through the scenic countryside. A stop at the rural settlement of Garston gave us a chance to stretch our legs before continuing on to Te Anau, where one of its downtown shops doubled as our business class lounge. The coffee and pastries that were waiting for me when I arrived in Te Anau were a lovely touch, and a thoughtful gesture by the tour operators. As we entered Fiordland National Park, part of the UNESCO World Heritage site Te Wahipounam, the scenery became increasingly breathtaking. The landscape shifted dramatically as the narrow road widened, revealing Eglinton Valley in all its glory. This expansive flat is a testament to the region's geological history, carved out by ancient glaciers that left behind a canvas of golden tussock grass and striking triangular peaks. Our journey continued with a visit to Mirror Lakes, where the Earl Mountains are perfectly reflected in the glassy waters. The stillness of the lake created an eerie sense of symmetry, as if the mountains were mirrored on its surface. Nearby, Falls Creek cascaded into a tranquil teal pond, a breathtaking contrast to the rugged landscape. As we stopped at Monkey Creek, our guide's sharp eyes spotted two kea perched in the trees. These alpine parrots are known for their playful behavior and mischievous nature, adding a touch of whimsy to our excursion. Their distinctive calls echoed through the valley as they flitted about, seemingly enjoying the attention. The Homer Tunnel loomed ahead, a narrow passage carved through the solid rock of Darran Mountain. As we emerged on the other side, our guide made a fitting adjustment to the soundtrack, switching to the iconic theme from Jurassic Park. The dramatic change in scenery was mirrored by the music, setting the tone for our arrival at Milford Sound. The descent into Cleddau Valley was a masterclass in scenic contrasts, with daunting granite walls giving way to the tranquil waters of the sound. Our final stop before boarding the MV Sinbad was a bridge offering a glimpse of Fiordland's highest peak, Mount Tūtuko, towering above us. As we settled into our table by the window, the expansive views of the surrounding peaks and waterfalls were matched by the warm hospitality of our hosts. A glass of Cloudy Bay wine was presented to us as a welcome gesture, setting the tone for the culinary journey ahead. The first course arrived promptly: a seeded sourdough bun with whipped kelp butter that provided a subtle yet intriguing start to the meal. This was followed by a rich and savory Fiordland wapiti bone broth soup, showcasing the local flavors of the region. The combination of textures and tastes was expertly balanced. The next series of dishes was designed to delight both the palate and the eye: three artfully plated bite-sized morsels that showcased the freshest ingredients from the area. Paua with black garlic made a striking impression, as did the crispy fried ball made of titi, while the roe from Mount Cook salmon added an elegant touch. As we savored each dish, our captain regaled us with stories about Milford Sound's breathtaking waterfalls, including Sutherland Falls, Lady Bowen Falls, and Stirling Falls. His commentary was both informative and engaging, adding a new layer of appreciation for this natural wonder. It wasn't until he mentioned the relatively modest height of Niagara Falls that I realized just how massive these cascades truly were. The penultimate dish was a masterful combination of wapiti tartare with potato crisps and smoked eel, each element complementing the others in perfect harmony. articles.title: Republican leaders struggle with post-election recovery amid Trump's continued dominance
articles.summary: GOP leaders are grappling with how to move forward after midterm losses, with opinions ranging from distancing themselves from President Donald Trump to embracing his involvement.
articles.content: Republican leaders are grappling with how to recover from their midterm losses, and one thing they agree on is that President Donald Trump will remain a dominant force in the party for now. State and county officials from across the country have shared their views on the future of the Republican Party since Election Day, revealing a party still reeling from its defeat. Some are eager to distance themselves from Trump's influence, while others see him as essential to the party's success. There is no consensus on how to move forward, with opinions ranging from wanting to dump Trump entirely to embracing his continued involvement. Despite their differences, all acknowledge that he will play a significant role in shaping the party's future. GOP leaders are acutely aware of the challenges ahead, particularly retaining control of the White House in two years' time, but they also recognize that Trump's influence cannot be ignored. The Republican Party's future hangs in the balance as President Trump's popularity plummets among voters. A recent poll has revealed that his approval rating stands at a mere 32% overall, with a staggering 70% of Republicans still backing him - a significant drop from the 91% he enjoyed on inauguration day last year. The survey also highlighted a growing divide within the party, as 56% of Trump's 2024 voters believe the Republican Party should distance itself from his agenda. This sentiment is not reflected in the actions of the party leadership, however. Despite this, some grassroots leaders are beginning to speak out against Trump's influence. A small but vocal group of Republicans has expressed their discontent with Trump's dominance over the party. Vermont GOP chair Paul Dame bluntly stated that he doesn't know how much [Trump] really has to offer. Meanwhile, Michael Bub, chair of Taylor County, Wisconsin's Republican Party, urged Trump to stay out of local politics: The Republican Party seems to be acknowledging that Trump's influence will continue to shape their electoral strategy, despite his divisive leadership style. Party officials are aware of Trump's ability to energize voters and expose Democratic weaknesses, which they believe is crucial for winning in 2024. However, some party leaders are pressing for a more constructive role from the president, rather than simply allowing him to dominate the narrative. State-level Republican leaders want Trump to take on a mentorship-like figure, guiding the party without exerting too much control over its direction. State-level Republican leaders are hesitant to assign blame directly to Trump for the party's current predicament. Some chairs have chosen not to engage in finger-pointing, deeming it an unproductive exercise that could hinder efforts to move forward. West Virginia GOP chair Josh Holstein exemplifies this approach, stating "I don't want to play the blame game" and instead focusing on finding solutions. This reluctance underscores the delicate balance party leaders must maintain when discussing Trump's role within the party. Many chairs have praised Trump's ability to attract new voters to the Republican Party, crediting him with efforts to mobilize these individuals on behalf of other candidates. GOP chairs in various states have acknowledged Trump's impact on voter turnout and his influence on the electoral landscape. While some hope for a change in leadership by 2028, allowing the party to choose its nominee without Trump's involvement. Oklahoma GOP chair Charity Linch expressed this sentiment, urging Republicans to move beyond the "Trump era and focus on selecting a new president. The 2028 Republican primaries are already shaping up to be a contentious affair, with some party leaders urging their colleagues to move beyond the shadow of former President Donald Trump. Even those who have chosen not to endorse his preferred candidate, state Senator Alex Gruters, still believe that Trump should play a significant role in the upcoming election cycle. Kentucky GOP chair Robert Benvenuti is among them, stating that Trump's leadership has been tremendous" for the country and that he should remain actively involved in 2024. Some party leaders are now advocating for a more balanced approach, suggesting that it would be premature to exclude Trump from the primaries altogether. articles.title: Hyundai Unveils Revamped Elantra Sedan at LA Auto Show
articles.summary: The Hyundai Elantra has been revamped with an economy-focused hybrid powertrain and AI voice assistant, promising improved fuel efficiency and a more engaging driving experience.
articles.content: Hyundai has unveiled its latest offerings at the LA Auto Show, and among them is a revamped Elantra sedan that's sure to turn heads. While opinions may vary on the car's bold styling, it's the economy-focused features that will likely draw in potential buyers. The compact hybrid sedan boasts an impressive targeted 53 mpg, making it an attractive option for those concerned about fuel costs. The Hyundai Elantra has long been a staple of the brand's lineup, and its importance cannot be overstated. As one of the company's best-selling vehicles, it ranks second only to the Tucson in terms of sales. Moreover, the Elantra occupies a crucial segment in the market, affordable compact sedans, which many US automakers have abandoned in favor of SUVs. In an era where buyers are increasingly sensitive to sticker prices and fuel costs, economy car options like the Elantra are worth taking note of. This is particularly true given the current market conditions, where buyers are seeking value for money more than ever before. The updated hybrid powertrain promises to deliver on this front, with a targeted 53 mpg that's sure to appeal to those looking to save on fuel. The new hybrid powertrain pairs a 1.6-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine with a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox. This combination results in a significant boost in combined output at the front wheels, rising to 155 horsepower from 139 hp in the current car. A more powerful electric-assist motor, now rated at 45 kilowatts, also contributes to this increase. As part of the updated powertrain, Hyundai's new AI voice assistant, Gleo, takes center stage. This innovative feature allows for seamless control over the automaker's Android Automotive OS-based dashboard technology. With its intuitive interface and advanced capabilities, Gleo promises to elevate the driving experience and provide users with a more engaging interaction with their vehicle. The updated regenerative braking system in the new Hyundai Elantra Hybrid now captures energy more efficiently when slowing down, allowing drivers to experience a "one-pedal driving experience" that can even bring the car to a complete stop at its maximum setting. This advanced feature is complemented by the introduction of Stay mode, which enables the climate control and infotainment systems to run for up to 30 minutes while parked without activating the gas engine. This eco-friendly function allows drivers to enjoy a range of amenities without wasting fuel. The non-hybrid Elantra model, also unveiled in LA, features the same 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine and continuously variable transmission as its predecessor. Despite being slightly more powerful than before, with a target of 35 mpg combined, it is expected to be just as efficient. The increased size of the sedan may even contribute to improved fuel efficiency. The interior design of the new Elantra Hybrid has been revamped, with the digital instrument cluster now situated on the dashboard near the windshield. This repositioning puts vital information within easy view for drivers, providing a more intuitive driving experience. The sleek design is reminiscent of recent Toyota models that have incorporated similar cockpit layouts. Pleos Connect, Hyundai's innovative infotainment suite, takes center stage on a 12.9-inch display screen. Based on Android Automotive OS, this system offers seamless integration with the driver's smartphone and features standard wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto connectivity. The user-friendly interface enables drivers to navigate their favorite apps on the road while enjoying over-the-air updates for added convenience. The new Hyundai Elantra Hybrid boasts an impressive 53 mpg fuel efficiency rating, making it an attractive option for environmentally conscious drivers. The sedan's interior is equipped with a range of innovative features, including Gleo AI, Hyundai's latest voice assistant technology. Gleo AI allows users to interact with the car using natural language commands, eliminating the need to physically touch the touchscreen while driving. This cutting-edge system includes contextual language support, multi-command capability, and zone-specific recognition, enabling it to understand who is speaking and where they are sitting in the vehicle. At the unveiling of the new Elantra Hybrid, Hyundai's senior vice president of product, Olabisi Boyle, emphasized that affordability doesn't have to mean sacrificing style or sophistication. The sedan's sleek design, featuring chunky flared fenders and a tall greenhouse, is certainly anything but bland. The Elantra's exterior design language, dubbed "Art of Steel," draws inspiration from Hyundai's recent SUVs, while its angular lines evoke the brand's N Vision 74 concept and hydrogen-fueled Nexo. The sedan's unique triangular rear windows add to its distinctive appearance. Measuring 188.8 inches bumper-to-bumper on a 108.3-inch wheelbase, the Elantra offers improved rear-passenger space, with 39.1 inches of legroom available on the second row. According to Hyundai designers, this generation's stretch has brought the sedan's interior volume closer to that of a midsize car. Multiple attendees who exceeded six feet in height were able to comfortably fit into the back seat, suggesting that Hyundai's claims about increased interior space may be more than just marketing hype. The new Hyundai Elantra Hybrid made a splash at its auto show debut, but one thing was noticeably absent: pricing details. Hyundai's silence on this topic suggests that they're keeping their options open for now, allowing them to adjust prices according to market conditions. Availability of the 2027 Elantra sedan is expected to begin in early 2027, with the hybrid model likely following suit in late 2027. The exact timing may vary depending on several factors, including production schedules and distribution channels. articles.title: OpenAI Rolls Out ChatGPT Wallet Feature with Human Oversight Requirements
articles.summary: The feature allows AI agents to make payments on behalf of users, but requires human approval before finalization.
articles.content: OpenAI has rolled out ChatGPT Wallet, a feature allowing its AI agents to make payments on behalf of users, but these transactions still require human oversight before being finalized. While this safeguard may provide some initial security, it's ultimately a limitation that hinders the true potential of agentic payments. For an agent to be truly effective, it should be able to make decisions independently, without needing constant human approval at every stage. The technology behind agentic payments is rapidly advancing, with significant progress made in integrating existing payment methods into AI systems. However, there remains a crucial question that has yet to be addressed: what are the limits of an agent's decision-making authority? For instance, consider a scenario where an AI agent is tasked with planning a family vacation within a set budget. The agent books flights, hotels, and other arrangements without issue, but ultimately delivers a trip that falls short of the user's expectations. The issue of accountability arises when AI agents fail to deliver as expected, leaving users wondering who is responsible for their decisions. This problem persists even when merchants and payment providers follow existing dispute procedures, which may offer some remedies but do not clearly assign blame. Authorization to spend does not necessarily mean authorization to exercise judgment, a distinction that current infrastructure fails to recognize. The industry has begun to develop verifiable mandates to address this gap, with Google's Agent Payments Protocol being one notable example. This protocol uses cryptographically signed mandates to record user requests and approvals, but it only addresses half the problem. A signature can prove what was authorized, but it cannot confirm whether the agent interpreted the user's preferences correctly or acted in their best interest. Verifying an AI agent's actions is not a straightforward task. It requires three key layers of verification: mandates that capture intent, mechanisms to enforce those intentions, and safeguards against outside incentives. Mandates that encode intent are essential for verifiable transactions. They should include the user's priorities, trade-offs, and conditions for escalation, such as requiring permission before making non-refundable purchases. These constraints must be verifiable across the transaction, involving multiple parties without compromising user privacy. Ensuring AI agents act in accordance with their mandates is a complex challenge that demands innovative solutions. By developing more robust mechanisms to verify agent actions, the industry can build trust and confidence in these emerging technologies. To resolve disputes arising from agent actions, a clear liability framework must be established. This framework would determine which party bears responsibility when an agent acts within its spending authority but outside its intended purpose. Currently, ambiguity in instructions or misinterpretation by the provider can lead to losses for various stakeholders, including users, providers, merchants, and payment processors. The allocation of liability should be settled beforehand, ideally by identifying the party that can prevent harm at the lowest cost. This approach has been successfully implemented in other industries, such as the card industry's EMV liability shift, which incentivized merchants to adopt chip technology to reduce counterfeit-fraud losses. A similar principle is applied in product liability law, where defects are allocated along the supply chain. By establishing clear allocation of risk, it becomes possible to price and insure risks that can be assigned. This market creation enables stakeholders to manage and mitigate potential losses. In the context of AI-powered agents, a duty of loyalty must also be considered. Currently, OpenAI does not take a commission on Wallet transactions, but business models can evolve over time. As an agent's platform earns revenue from merchants through fees or advertising, it may face conflicts of interest that are invisible to users. These conflicts can be mitigated by enforcing standards for consumer agents, including disclosure requirements and best-interest obligations. Independent verification mechanisms must also be in place to ensure compliance with the user's mandate. The development of agentic protocols is underway in AI labs, payment companies, and commerce platforms. These entities are well-positioned to create private standards for identity verification, credentials, and payment flows due to the benefits of interoperability for all parties involved. As someone who has worked on both sides of regulatory rulebooks, it's clear that settling liability in advance is crucial for systems to scale. articles.title: French Healthcare System Offers Support for New Mothers
articles.summary: I made the bold decision to leave my life in the US behind and relocate to France when I met and married a French man at a dinner party in Chicago.
articles.content: I made the bold decision to leave my life in the US behind and relocate to France when I met and married a French man at a dinner party in Chicago. Our love for each other and his family led me to want to experience the rich culture of France firsthand and immerse myself in the French language. Initially, our move was meant to be temporary, lasting only two years, but life had other plans as we settled into a new home and started building a life together. The pandemic changed everything when I became pregnant; it suddenly made sense for us to stay in France and start a family there. As a soon-to-be mother, I was anxious about navigating the healthcare system in a foreign country. The hospital stay for my newborn son Philippe was extended due to his weight loss. The medical staff wanted to keep a close eye on him for six days before discharging me and my baby. During this time, I received assistance from the midwives who helped with caring for Philippe throughout the day. They provided guidance on essential tasks like feeding, bathing, and changing diapers. This support gave me confidence in my ability to care for my child once we left the hospital. The generous meal I was served during my stay, complete with Camembert and Black Forest Cake, was a welcome surprise. What's more, I didn't have to pay for it. In contrast, some of my friends back in the US had expressed concerns about affording the costs associated with pregnancy and parenthood. The expenses related to caring for an infant, from baby furniture to diapers, clothes, and other necessities, are significantly lower here in France compared to what I've heard is typical in the US. The transition from day care to formal education in France is a seamless one for Philippe's peers. At two-and-a-half years old, he started attending école maternelle, which provides pre-primary education to children aged 3 to 5. This system has been around since the 19th century and was officially incorporated into the French education system in 2019. However, by that time, an impressive 97% of students were already enrolled. The rate of enrollment is now at a remarkable 100%, making France a leader in pre-primary education within the EU. The food served at école maternelle is just as impressive as the educational experience itself. Children are treated to hourlong lunches, carefully prepared and presented on ceramic plates. The menu features a variety of dishes, with prices ranging from $1 to $5 per day, depending on the parents' income level. École maternelle places great emphasis on teaching children essential social skills, promoting their development as conscientious citizens and friends. Activities such as reading and writing are also encouraged, all within the context of a completely free education system. The cost of childcare in France is significantly lower compared to what American families face. For instance, a full-time aftercare program for our child costs just under $25 per week, which translates to around $5 per day. France's educational system also offers children regular breaks throughout the year, including an eight-week summer holiday that's shorter than its US counterpart. This means we don't have to worry about finding expensive childcare solutions during these periods. In fact, local recreation centers offer all-day programs in the summer, providing a range of activities and sports for kids. These municipal-run programs are priced based on income, making them an attractive option for working parents like us. We paid around $15 per day for our child's enrollment in one such program this summer, which worked out to about two weeks' worth of care. Splitting the remaining days between grandparents, family time, and specialized camps kept costs under $1,000 for the entire summer. As our child grows older, we're discovering that extracurricular activities in France are also remarkably affordable. This is a welcome change from what we experienced in the US, where such expenses can quickly add up. The cost of extracurricular activities for our child is significantly lower here in France. We pay under $200 a year for Judo classes, a expense that would likely be much higher back home. This is a welcome change from the financial burden we'd face in the US. While prices for everyday items and childcare costs are indeed lower in France compared to the United States, our salaries don't quite match those of our American counterparts. The trade-off seems fair to us, though, we're saving money on living expenses but earning less overall. It's a delicate balance that we've grown accustomed to. We're not planning to return to the US anytime soon, as our child has become deeply immersed in the French education system and switching schools would be complicated. In fact, university tuition fees here are also more manageable than what we'd face back home, about $1,200 a year compared to the potential $240,000 bill for an American college. articles.title: Aging Population in Maine Highlights Need for Support Services
articles.summary: Maine has an aging population that is among the oldest in the nation, which is why organizations like AgeMaine provide vital support services for older adults and their caregivers.
articles.content: Maine has an aging population that is among the oldest in the nation, which is why organizations like AgeMaine provide vital support services for older adults and their caregivers. The reality of family caregiving hit close to home when I saw a viral sketch on Saturday Night Live featuring a character known as "Sister. While it was initially intended as humor, it struck a chord with me because I see countless versions of this same scenario unfolding every day in Maine. For many families, the demands of caring for an aging loved one can be overwhelming. Siblings must juggle work commitments with coordinating appointments and medical care, while spouses provide around-the-clock support at home without formal training or respite. Caregiving is a common but often invisible burden that affects countless individuals and families in our society, from those providing care to parents to those caring for children while also managing the needs of an elderly relative. Navigating caregiving responsibilities can be overwhelming, especially when it comes to knowing where to turn for support. Families often find themselves in this situation unexpectedly, such as when a parent falls and requires immediate attention. In these moments, it's essential to have a plan in place. The reality is that many caregivers are forced to make significant sacrifices, including putting their careers on hold or depleting their retirement savings. This can have long-term consequences for not only the caregiver but also the family as a whole. It's crucial to recognize the economic, social, and emotional impact of caregiving on families. Caregivers often face questions about what steps to take next when caring for an aging parent, such as how to navigate healthcare systems or manage daily tasks. Families may feel uncertain about their ability to provide adequate care, leading to stress and anxiety. As organizations like AgeMaine emphasize the importance of early planning and prevention, it's clear that addressing caregiving needs requires a comprehensive approach that considers not just individual families but also broader societal implications. It's essential for adult children to initiate conversations about aging parents' care needs well in advance. This involves having an open discussion with family members, including parents, siblings, and spouses, to clarify their preferences and plans. Asking the right questions can help families navigate this complex issue. For instance, Have you considered what life looks like if you need more care?" encourages parents to think critically about their future needs and desires. By doing so, they can begin making informed decisions about their long-term care. Having a family discussion also allows siblings to identify their unique strengths and contributions. Some may excel at managing financial paperwork, while others might be better suited for regular visits or coordinating home health services. By acknowledging each sibling's role, families can work together more effectively and ensure that everyone is contributing positively. By starting this conversation early on, families can establish a clear understanding of their roles and responsibilities, making it easier to address caregiving needs as they arise. This proactive approach helps prevent last-minute decisions and ensures that family members are prepared to support one another throughout the aging process. As people age in America, many consider nursing homes or assisted living facilities as the primary solution for care. However, research suggests that most older adults prefer to stay in their own communities at home. To support this goal, families can think about what additional resources and services would enable a loved one to remain at home. This involves considering not just paid help with daily tasks like laundry and cooking, but also unpaid assistance from neighbors or community members. For example, weekly grocery shopping or transportation to appointments could be arranged. The key is to be intentional about where the individual lives and think long-term about their needs. Family members often unintentionally undermine their loved one's independence by treating them like children again. It's essential to remember that aging adults have valuable life experience, knowledge, and expertise, no one knows them better than themselves. By giving them choices and respecting their autonomy, families can preserve their dignity and well-being. Involving the individual in decision-making is crucial, as it allows them to maintain control over their lives. This proactive approach helps prevent last-minute decisions that may not align with their preferences or values. It's essential to involve aging parents in decision-making processes from an early stage, rather than leaving it for later when a crisis arises. This proactive approach helps ensure that older adults are not forced into situations that don't align with their preferences or values. Older individuals have unique insights and priorities that should be taken into account when making decisions about their care. By including them in the conversation, families can gain a better understanding of what matters most to their loved ones. This shared understanding enables more informed choices to be made. Caregivers often overlook their own health and wellness while focusing on stabilizing their aging loved one's situation. It's crucial for caregivers to prioritize their own needs as well, in order to provide the best possible support to both themselves and their loved one. Building a supportive team is essential for managing the complex responsibilities involved in caregiving. Caregivers should also take steps to understand the financial landscape of their aging loved one, including documentation of wishes, powers of attorney, wills, and insurance coverage. By being aware of available resources and having a grasp of the paperwork involved, families can avoid unnecessary stress and make more informed decisions about care and support. Having multiple resources available from the outset is crucial for families caring for aging parents. This not only helps in emergency situations but also ensures that loved ones stay connected socially, addressing both physical and social health needs. Regular check-ins and visits can be a vital part of this support system. Key members of the team might include neighbors or friends who can stop by for coffee, notice if a parent hasn't been out for a few days, or suggest ways to bring purpose and joy into their lives. These individuals can help maintain social connections, which are essential for healthy aging not just for parents but also for family caregivers. Ultimately, having a support network in place helps families navigate the challenges of caring for aging loved ones with greater ease and confidence, ensuring that both physical and emotional needs are met. articles.title: Male Influencers Gather for Grappling Session at Retreat in Denver
articles.summary: A group of male influencers gathered for an intense grappling session as part of a weeklong retreat aimed at teaching men and boys to embody healthy masculinity.
articles.content: In a recent gathering at Hey Brother House in suburban Denver, a group of male influencers gathered for an intense grappling session. The event was part of a weeklong retreat aimed at teaching men and boys to embody healthy masculinity. Carlos Monteon Jr., a wrestler and influencer from Arizona, was among the participants. Monteon, known for his impressive physique and large following on TikTok and Instagram, was demonstrating a wrestling technique called "riding to a group of eight men watching in a circle. The technique involves controlling the opponent while straddling them. Monteon's demo partner, Johnny Cole, a content creator with a substantial social media presence, was the recipient of this instruction. The grappling session ended with Monteon on top of Cole, their faces inches apart and their torsos glistening with sweat. This intense display of physicality was not unlike a junior varsity wrestling match, complete with cameramen capturing every move from various angles. A drone hovered above the scene, adding to the sense of drama. The retreat, which also included other activities like meditation and emotional processing, aimed to promote healthy masculinity among young men. Hey Brother House's mission is to create content that will positively influence social media feeds and encourage positive change in 18-to-25-year-old men. The project has received significant funding from the Young Men and Media Collective. The retreat was being documented by a filmmaker, Matthew Echelman, who had hired two crew members to capture the events for potential use in a future documentary. The goal of this documentation is to showcase the impact of Hey Brother House's approach on its participants. The project seeks to address issues of toxic masculinity and promote more positive role models among young men. The retreat's founder, Johnny Cole, is part of a team that includes two other house leaders at Hey Brother House. Their work involves creating content and experiences aimed at promoting healthy relationships between men and their emotions. The rented stucco McMansion on the outskirts of Denver's Green Valley Ranch Golf Club community serves as a unique gathering space for a group of young men. The house is equipped with various amenities that cater to their interests, including a Nintendo Switch console in the living room where they can play Mario Kart. A basement area is dedicated to fitness, featuring equipment such as air hockey and Foosball tables. The Man Box within the house is a designated space for testimonials, where members share their thoughts on camera about their daily experiences. This setup bears some resemblance to reality TV formats, but with a distinct twist: the individuals involved are aware of bell hooks' work on love and relationships, and they explicitly aim to form friendships. A stroll through the property reveals an atmosphere that is both familiar and peculiar. Young men from various walks of life have converged in Denver, drawn by concerns about the struggles faced by their demographic. Cole, one of the members, reflects on these issues while smoking Marlboro Lights on the porch. Men and boys are not doing well, he notes. The evidence supporting this assertion is multifaceted. Data indicates that young men are less likely than their female counterparts to complete high school and pursue higher education. They also tend to drop out of the job market, experience increased rates of loneliness and isolation, and have a higher likelihood of succumbing to suicidal tendencies. A contributing factor to these problems is the manosphere, an online ecosystem inhabited by various groups, including looksmaxxers, incels, AI-touting hustle bros, and peptide-injecting fitness influencers. Initially a fringe coalition, this collective has grown in influence due to the popularity of certain high-profile figures. The success of individuals like Jordan Peterson, who has advocated for all-meat diets and climate-change denialism, and Andrew Tate, a former kickboxer facing numerous charges in the UK and Romania, including trafficking and sex crimes, has helped propel the manosphere into mainstream relevance. The rise of traditional masculinity as a path to self-empowerment has been amplified by social media algorithms, which have helped influencers like Tate reach an enormous audience. By 2023, clips featuring him had garnered over 13 billion views on various platforms, with some of his content being shared and consumed by millions of young men disillusioned by the rise of identity politics. This demographic's voting habits in the 2024 election were notable, with an estimated 67 percent of white male zoomers casting their ballots for Trump, sparking a flurry of discussions about the manosphere's influence on young men's frustrations. The lack of brotherhood and friendship among this group is a pressing issue, according to Cole, who is working to reach them through his project Hey Brother House. As one of the leaders of the house, Cole stands out from his peers due to his demographic: he's 6'4, built like an athlete, with striking features that set him apart from others in the group. Cole sees his work as a calling, driven by a desire to help young men who have never experienced genuine brotherhood or male friendship before. He believes that by adopting the visual hallmarks of the manosphere, slick editing and dynamic hooks, and applying them to content promoting healthy masculinity, he can reach and inspire this neglected demographic. The Hey Brother House aims to rebrand the concept of healthy masculinity for social media influencers. By promoting values such as empathy and vulnerability, Cole hopes to attract a younger demographic that's been neglected by existing content creators. This approach is a departure from more traditional methods, which often involve lecturing young men about the evils of patriarchy. Many online platforms offer content for young men that focuses on positive activities like fitness or style advice. However, much of this material is either overly academic or infused with feminist terminology, which may alienate its intended audience. Cole and his team are trying to find a middle ground by creating content that's both engaging and relevant. The Hey Brother House has selected eight male influencers to participate in their program, all of whom have a strong online presence but don't exclusively focus on politics. This diverse group includes premed students, trainers, artists, and dancers who have varying levels of experience working with brands. Their goal is to create content that promotes healthy masculinity without being preachy or alienating. One of the participants in the program is Mars Wright, a trans man and artist who has never lived with cis men before. He expressed some trepidation about joining the group, likening it to entering a high school social scene from a popular teen movie. His concerns reflect the challenges that come with trying to redefine what healthy masculinity means on social media. In selecting participants for the Hey Brother House, Cole and his team had to strike a delicate balance between finding creators who align with their mission and avoiding those who only make content focused on politics. This was no easy task, given the large number of applicants, over 130 men vied for a spot in the program. The team chose influencers who have existing audiences but are not strictly limited to one niche or topic. For example, Sean Jones makes date-night videos and productivity vlogs, while Stephen Marmolejos posts fitness content and does sponsorships with brands like Corona and Thayers. The atmosphere is charged with emotion as the group gathers for an intimate conversation. The men are seated in a circle, some visibly moved by the shared experience. This is a rare moment of vulnerability, especially for those who have traditionally been associated with a more macho image. Cole's words of encouragement are met with nods and affirmations from the group. He emphasizes the importance of revealing one's feelings as a crucial step towards healing. The men seem to absorb his message, their body language conveying a sense of openness and trust. articles.title: Wolf Behavior Study Reveals Social Dynamics as Primary Driver of Howling
articles.summary: Research suggests that social dynamics are the primary driver behind wolf howling behavior, rather than the full moon.
articles.content: Wolves are renowned for their haunting howls, which can travel far and wide across vast landscapes. The sound is so distinctive that it has become an integral part of popular culture. However, what triggers this behavior in wolves remains a topic of interest among experts. Contrary to the widespread notion that the full moon sparks wolf howling, research suggests that social dynamics are the primary driver behind this behavior. According to experts, wolves engage in vocalizations as a means to maintain complex relationships within their groups. A lone wolf's howl is likely an attempt to reconnect with its pack, while those that have left their packs may use howling as a way to find new companions or mates. The possibility of attracting a partner or joining another group seems to be a motivating factor in these instances. Experts point out that wolf packs often use howling as a means to advertise their territory and deter other packs from encroaching on their domain. The data indicates that packs are more likely to engage in this behavior when they are situated at the center of their territory, have young pups nearby, or have recently secured a successful hunt. In these situations, howling may serve multiple purposes for the wolf pack, including signaling its presence and reinforcing social bonds within the group. When wolves gather together and let out a chorus of howls, it's often a social exercise designed to foster a sense of unity within the pack. This collective behavior is thought to strengthen bonds between individual members, creating a feeling of safety in numbers. The process works both ways: hearing another wolf's howl can trigger an instinctual response in the listener to join in and reply with their own vocalizations. In fact, researchers suggest that this phenomenon is so strong that even if a lone wolf stumbles into a neighboring pack's territory by mistake, it won't respond to the group's collective howling. The sheer distance that howls can travel is also noteworthy, up to 10 miles in open terrain, according to some estimates. This range allows packs to communicate with one another over vast expanses, potentially even warning off potential intruders or signaling the presence of a rival pack. Wolf pups take their first tentative steps into howling at an early age, typically between two and four weeks old, when they begin experimenting with high-pitched vocalizations. The distinctive sound of a wolf's howl is not unique to any one species or subspecies. Research has shown that each type of wolf, from timber wolves to red wolves, has its own distinct howling dialect. These howling dialects feature different types of howls with varying regularity depending on the specific species or subspecies. For instance, the timber wolf's repertoire is characterized by low, flat howls, while red wolves are more likely to produce high, looping howls. Not all canines howl in the same way as wolves, however. Dogs, which are descended from gray wolves, may have a different howling style depending on their breed. Some dog breeds that are more closely related to wolves tend to howl more frequently than others. Studies suggest that even within dog breeds, there is a correlation between an animal's genetic closeness to wolves and its tendency to howl. More ancient breeds, which are more genetically similar to wolves, may be more likely to engage in howling behavior. Researchers investigating why wolves howl have been exploring whether the sounds they make vary depending on their purpose. According to one expert, these differences might be audible in the pitch and tone of the howls. The idea that wolves howl at the moon is a common myth that has been debunked by scientists. When a wolf is feeling threatened during a territorial conflict, its howl may have a distinct pattern compared to when it's relaxed. articles.title: Nonprofit Fundraising Platform DonorPerfect Takes Systems Offline Due to Cyberattack Threats
articles.summary: DonorPerfect took its systems offline on November 10 after detecting attempted cyberattacks, leaving 11,000 customers without access to their accounts.
articles.content: A major nonprofit fundraising platform has taken drastic measures to protect itself from cyberattacks just days before one of the busiest giving seasons of the year. DonorPerfect, a popular software and CRM platform for nonprofits, made the difficult decision to go offline on November 10 as attacks were being attempted on its systems. According to Lauren Sheehan, president of DonorPerfect, the decision was taken in a state of high alert, likening it to being in the Situation Room during a crisis. "We're like, 'just take it down, so that we know that they can't get through,'" she explained, describing the company's actions as a preemptive security measure. The temporary shutdown left DonorPerfect's 11,000 customers without access to their accounts right before what's historically the busiest time of year for nonprofits. Nonprofits rely heavily on this period to raise funds, and December is particularly crucial, with online revenue peaking during the last two to three months of the year. The impact of the shutdown was not limited to DonorPerfect alone. Many nonprofits that use the platform were left scrambling to find alternative ways to manage their fundraising efforts. Sheehan acknowledged the difficulties faced by these organizations, saying it's "really difficult to tell your 11,000 customers that their system isn't available." The company has engaged cybersecurity experts to investigate the unauthorized activity and put protective measures in place to prevent further attacks. The investigation is ongoing, with DonorPerfect assessing whether customer information was accessed without authorization during the breach. DonorPerfect's decision to take its systems offline was met with understanding from customers who recognized that the move was made out of an abundance of caution. The company had wanted to ensure that all systems were safe before putting them back online, and it's likely that this approach will be scrutinized in the aftermath of the incident. Several major companies, including Microsoft, suffered significant disruptions around the same time as DonorPerfect's outage. These incidents have raised questions about whether they are related. The fact that DonorPerfect has confirmed unauthorized activity involving certain systems sets its incident apart from other outages. While some companies may downplay the severity of their issues or offer vague explanations, DonorPerfect chose to be transparent and proactive in addressing the problem. GoFundMe Pro, a platform used by nonprofit customers, also reported a security incident that resulted in unauthorized access. A spokesperson for GoFundMe Pro suggested that bad actors are targeting fundraising platforms serving the nonprofit sector, and it remains to be seen whether other companies will face similar attacks. GoFundMe has disclosed that sensitive information from its customers was compromised in a recent cyberattack. The accessed data includes names, postal addresses, email addresses, phone numbers, and dates of birth of donors and supporters for affected organizations. The breach also involved access to credentials for GoFundMe Pro's Salesforce integration, potentially allowing attackers to view records in the platform. Affected organizations may need to take additional steps to secure their accounts. Nonprofit fundraising platforms are facing a difficult time ahead of Giving Tuesday, with multiple high-profile attacks in recent weeks. The incidents have left some wondering whether other companies will be targeted. Donor trust is already a concern for nonprofits, as they strive to build credibility and demonstrate effective use of funds. According to a report by Bloomerang, 85% of active donors trust the organizations they donate to, but this trust can be eroded by scam activity. DonorPerfect's online donation forms are back up after a recent cyberattack, but some services remain offline. A few integrations, including its API, which is used for partner connections, are still unavailable, causing some inconvenience to customers who use these features. Sheehan explained that donations made through partners like GoFundMe are being processed normally and safely, but the data from these transactions isn't automatically transferred into DonorPerfect's system. Customers must manually import and export this information. The forensic investigation into the attack is ongoing, and Sheehan emphasized that her team can't provide further details until it's completed. She noted a delicate balance between resolving the issue quickly and doing so correctly to ensure that all security protocols are in place. DonorPerfect has been voluntarily sharing its monitoring logs and details about security incidents with competitors and partners in the nonprofit sector via email. The company's willingness to collaborate on this level is unusual, according to Sheehan, who emphasized that the health of the industry takes precedence over individual companies' interests. articles.content: TJX, parent company of discount retailers TJ Maxx and Marshalls, has allocated $167 million of its $463 million in tariff refunds towards bonuses for non-executive associates. This decision follows guidance from U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer who suggested in March that companies pass on refunds as a bonus or raise to their employees. A recent analysis by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York found that nearly 90% of the economic burden from tariffs fell on U.S. firms and consumers. Titleist-maker Acushnet and industrial tool producer Stanley Black & Decker have both disclosed plans to allocate millions of dollars returned from tariffs towards employee compensation packages. ProPublica has identified at least nine public companies that are following this trend, including those in the retail and manufacturing sectors. TJX, parent company of TJMaxx, has reported using $167 million of its $463 million in tariff refunds on compensation and bonuses, with this sum representing one-third of the total amount received by the firm. The money is being spent on year-end incentive compensation and discretionary bonuses for eligible employees globally. Stanley Black & Decker has also noted that its tariff refund gain was partially offset by variable incentive compensation costs and growth investments. The company's decision to allocate a portion of the funds towards taxes raises questions about the effectiveness of the rebate system in benefiting consumers directly. The allocation of tariff refunds by companies continues to raise concerns over corporate priorities and transparency. As some firms commit to passing on rebates or lowering prices, others seem to be using the money for internal purposes, leaving it unclear whether consumers will ultimately benefit from these rebates. As the Supreme Court's ruling on tariffs comes into effect, several American importers are set to receive reimbursement for over $166 billion in import taxes paid under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA). Economists point out that American households bore the brunt of the tariffs under IEEPA, with estimates suggesting that they paid around $1,000 more annually due to the trade restrictions. The distribution of tariff refunds by TJMaxx's parent company has raised eyebrows, with a significant portion allocated to corporate bonuses. Consumers have limited leverage over firms, Greenland noted, implying that companies may not prioritize refund distribution.
